body:
- **The exchange filing is the canonical source.** SEBI LODR (Reg 46 amendment 2021; Reg 30/Sch III amendment June 2023) requires transcripts on the company website and with the exchanges within 5 working days, and audio/video recordings promptly. The 2023 text says the next trading day or 24 h; secondary sources differ, so check the consolidated regulation. Sources: [Vinod Kothari guide](https://vinodkothari.com/2021/07/step-by-step-guide-for-disclosure-for-analysts-investors-meet/), [Khaitan 2023 note](https://www.khaitanco.com/sites/default/files/2023-06/SEBI%20enhances%20disclosure%20and%20governance%20requirements%20of%20listed%20entities_1.pdf).
- NSE: in the announcements JSON, filter `desc == "Analysts/Institutional Investor Meet/Con. Call Updates"` and `"ranscript" in attchmntText` (this catches typos like "ransacript"). KPITTECH had 17 such filings.
- BSE: `NEWSSUB` contains "Earnings Call Transcript".
- screener.in: the Concalls section is visible **without login**, with Transcript, PPT and REC links per quarter. Transcript links go to BSE `AnnPdfOpen`. AI Summary needs login. Good as a cross-check index of which quarters exist.
- Extraction: `pdftotext` (poppler) **is installed**. `pdftotext -layout` on KPIT Q2FY27 (20 pages) gave 8,530 words with speaker labels ("Kishor Patil:", "Moderator:"). That is enough to split management remarks from Q&A. Micro-cap scanned PDFs need OCR (tesseract, not tested).
- Sample promise found in the KPIT Q2FY27 call (28-Oct-2026), as an example of a tracker item: an analyst asked whether EBITDA margins would return to the 20–21% range. The CEO replied: "it will go up to some extent, every quarter, but, it will be early next year when we get there." Tracker entry: metric = EBITDA margin; target = about 20–21%; deadline = early CY2027; specificity = medium (range given, date vague); check each quarter's result.

In late 2025/2026 the Cabinet froze ~Rs 87,695 cr AGR dues with repayment from FY32 (later reassessed lower), and ABG committed ~Rs 4,730 cr via warrants (May-2026; Rs 1,183 cr received Jun-2026, single-source). (3) Hindalco's big leveraged Novelis buys (2007, Aleris 2020). Good conduct: clean ABCL-ABFL merger (2024), ABFRL demerger, UltraTech's acquisitions largely accretive. Status Nov-2026: no regulator actions found; key risk is Vi funding calls.

body:
**Universe (fixed).** NSE main-board equities with market cap ₹500 cr–₹50,000 cr at the entry date. Market cap
= shares outstanding (best available point-in-time source; approximation documented in §1) × close.
Exclude: banks/NBFCs/insurers are **kept** (EPS-based SUE works for them) but reported as a subset;
exclude stocks with < 250 days of price history before entry; exclude EPS series with gaps that prevent
the SUE computation. If full-universe data is infeasible, a seeded random sample of ≥ 300 companies from the
NSE equity list is used, and the report says so.

**Size-matched controls (H2).** For each event, control return = equal-weight mean return over the
identical window of all *sampled* universe stocks with mcap within ×0.5–×2 of the event firm on the entry
date (excluding the event firm; require ≥ 5 controls). Excess = event return − control return.

**Coverage proxy (H3).** Mcap tertile of the event firm, cut points recomputed each fiscal quarter among that
quarter's eligible events.

**Sample periods.** Train = announcements 2018-01-01 → 2021-12-31; Test = 2022-01-01 → 2025-12-31.
Both are reported; **the verdict is based on the test period**.

**Inference.** Unit = fiscal quarter (16 train, 16 test). Mean of quarterly T−B, t-stat across quarters
(Newey–West not needed at 63d since quarters barely overlap; reported naive across-quarter t), and a
**95% bootstrap CI resampling quarters** (5,000 draws). Event-level means also reported for context.

**Decision rules (pre-committed).**
1. Train-period result with **t < 3 will not be called an edge** (Harvey–Liu–Zhu), whatever its sign.
2. "Edge candidate" requires: test-period 63d T−B bootstrap CI excludes 0 (positive), **and** same sign as
   train, **and** top-vs-controls (H2) net of a 1% round-trip cost still > 0 with CI excluding 0 for a
   long-only version. Otherwise: "not established".
3. H3 "supported" only if the small-tertile T−B minus large-tertile T−B is > 0 in both periods with the test
   CI of the difference excluding 0.
4. Costs: report gross and net of 0.5% and 1.0% round trip (T−B long-short = two round trips; India shorting
   of cash equities over 3 months is not practical for retail, so the long-only H2 is the practical test).

**Everything else is exploratory** (revenue SUE, deciles, next-day open entry, sector, year-by-year,
both-beat EPS+revenue, Friday/crowded-day effects) and must be re-tested before it is believed.

**Survivorship plan.** Current NSE equity list misses delisted/merged firms. Count sampled firms with
truncated price history, and bound the effect under stated assumptions.

body:
- **Subsidiaries:** Fasttel (Brazil) was to hold 7-8% EBITDA (Feb-25) and break even in FY26 (May-25). Outcome: INR 186 cr EBITDA loss in 9M FY26, called "a setback for us" when asked (Feb-26), then a **INR 515 cr standalone provision** and exit from Brazil in Q4FY26.
- **Dates for asset sales and collections slip 1-2 quarters:**
  - VEPL road sale: "by Q2" (Feb-25), "Q2, Q3" (May-25), "Q3" (Aug-25), "H2" (Oct-25); closed Jan-26.
  - Indore real estate: INR 130 cr "in 60-90 days" (May-25) and INR 100 cr "Q2 or early Q3, not beyond that" (Aug-25); INR 75 cr still due at Dec-25; collected by Mar-26.
  - JJM water receivables: 60-70% of ~INR 1,500 cr to "start coming from June/Q2" (May-25). Instead receivables rose to INR 1,551 cr by Sep-25 and were ~1,600 cr in May-26. FY26 water collections were INR 1,800 cr against INR 2,500 cr invested.
- **Capex overspent every guide:** "below FY25" (Feb-25), INR 600-650 cr (May-25), 600-700 (Aug-25), 700-750 (Feb-26); actual "nearly INR 900 cr". Framed each time as growth investment funded from cash flow.
- **Oil & Gas** +55% vs "+100%+"; **international T&D inflow** ~INR 8,000 cr vs 9,500-10,000 (84%); **T&D inflow** ~INR 13,000 cr vs "better than FY25's 14,461" (90%); India T&D inflow fell from ~7,000 to ~4,500 cr.
- **The mid-year raise.** In Oct-25 FY26 revenue guidance was raised to "25%+", and in Feb-26 restated as "approx 25%". Delivered 22-23% (partly). In May-26 management listed its FY26 targets as "revenue growth of 20% to 25%" and said it had "fully delivered on each of these promises". The raise was not mentioned.
- **Railways:** an international railway win was expected in Q2-Q3 FY26; none was reported. International water: "a few significant wins in FY26"; the first (INR 344 cr, Middle East) came in Q1FY27.

body:
1. **Mechanical edges in public data are mostly arbitraged away** (McLean–Pontiff confirmed in our own tests).
   Our durable, cheap advantage is on the **defensive side**: avoid stocks after big earnings misses; avoid or size
   small high-pledge / insolvent-looking firms. Avoiding blow-ups compounds as surely as finding winners.
2. **Offensive edge must come from depth, not rules**: reading what others skip (filings, footnotes, concalls
   across years), management credibility over time, and the user's ground checks. These are expensive for humans
   and cheap for us — that asymmetry is the real edge thesis ("Lynch at scale").
3. **Proof comes only from forward scoring.** 115 dated calls resolve Jan–Jul 2027. Until then: no idea-pitching.
